profile.campus: Hillsboro, Oregon (Flexential's Hillsboro data center campus, four existing buildings plus a fifth completed and a sixth planned as of 2025)

profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential Portland - Hillsboro 4 Expansion) is located at 4915 NE Starr Blvd, Hillsboro, OR 97124. The operator publishes a footprint of 138000 square feet and 36 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including HITRUST CSF, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, NIST 800-53, ITAR, SSAE 18. This building is part of Flexential's wider Hillsboro campus, which Data Center Dynamics reported in 2025 had grown to five sites (four existing buildings plus Hillsboro 5, then under construction) totaling 1.18 million square feet and 113 megawatts of capacity, with a sixth facility then being planned across from Hillsboro 1 at 350,000 square feet and 27 megawatts. Flexential president and COO Ryan Mallory described Hillsboro as "a smart alternative to Silicon Valley for customers seeking the performance, flexibility, and cost structure they can't find elsewhere, especially those with strong ties across the Pacific." DCD also reported that the Hillsboro market ran extremely tight in the first half of 2025, with a vacancy rate of just 0.2% and 48.4 megawatts of absorption against 48 megawatts of new supply delivered, roughly 10% of total market inventory turning over in six months. Hillsboro sits in Oregon's "Silicon Forest" technology corridor west of Portland, built up around Intel's long-standing local manufacturing presence and the skilled workforce it created, a legacy that has also drawn other major data center operators, including Meta, to the same area.

The City of Hillsboro reports that, as of July 2026, the city hosted 23 total data center sites, 16 already constructed across 346 acres plus 7 more in permitting or under construction across another 224 acres, together occupying roughly 570 of the city's 17,378 total acres. In 2025, Hillsboro's data center sector generated about $61.1 million in total taxes; 12 entities receiving Enterprise Zone property-tax abatements held roughly $7.2 billion in exempted real market value, out of an $11 billion combined assessed/exempted value across all data centers in the city. Eligible facilities receive temporary property-tax abatement on new investment for three to five years under Hillsboro's Enterprise Zone program, after which standard property taxes apply, alongside application fees capped at $50,000 and Community Service Fees of up to 33% of abated taxes in the first three years. Statewide, Oregon's data center industry supported an estimated 9,310 direct jobs and 38,380 indirect and induced jobs, with more than $4.1 billion in labor income, in 2023, according to industry analysis cited by the city.

reading.body:
Flexential's Hillsboro 4 expansion in Portland publishes 36 MW of IT capacity today with 54 MW of additional critical capacity planned, positioning it as the fourth-largest published data center campus in Oregon by capacity. The facility sits in a 138,000 square foot footprint with a larger 358,000 square foot technical footprint, suggesting significant room for further buildout. At 40 kW per rack as a common density for mixed workloads, the 36 MW current capacity represents roughly 900 racks, with the planned 54 MW expansion potentially adding 1,350 racks; together these would make roughly 2,250 racks or equivalently 18,000 H100-equivalent accelerators at four accelerators per kilowatt.

The campus holds certifications for security compliance including HITRUST CSF, PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type II, NIST 800-53, and ITAR, as well as attestations for audit readiness including SOC 1 Type II, SOC 3, and SSAE 18. These certifications qualify the facility to host regulated workloads including government-classified work and financial services, but do not indicate which tenants are present. Oregon publishes only eight data center campuses with disclosed capacity across 133 mapped facilities statewide, for a total of 156.6 MW of published capacity; Hillsboro 4 represents 23 percent of the state's disclosed supply in existing capacity alone.

The campus is not published as grid-connected to a specific utility or power source, and planned expansion timing is not specified. Whether the planned 54 MW expansion depends on new power infrastructure or draws from existing supply in the Portland area is not disclosed by the operator.
